story.en: Snapchat HQ, product review Monday. The growth team pulls up the dashboard: 'We're seeing different engagement patterns across age groups — but are users spending more time sending snaps or opening them?' Analyst Priya has the activities log and user age data. Time to find out.
story.ta: Snapchat HQ, Monday product review. Growth team dashboard pull up pannaaanga: 'Different age groups-la different engagement patterns — but users snap send panrathula time more spend panraangala, open panrathula-a?' Analyst Priya-kita activities log-um user age data-um irukku. Kaandum.
story.hi: Snapchat HQ, Monday product review. Growth team ne dashboard khola: 'Alag age groups mein alag engagement pattern dikh raha hai — par users zyada time snap bhejne mein lagaate hain ya kholne mein?' Analyst Priya ke paas activities log aur user age data hai. Dekhte hain.
story.te: Snapchat HQ, Monday product review. Growth team dashboard tipiindi: 'Veru veru age groups lo veru engagement patterns kanipistunnaayi — kaani users snap pamputaniki ekkuva time spend chestunnaara, telupataniki-a?' Analyst Priya daggara activities log mariyu user age data undi. Chuddam.

question.en: For each age group, calculate the percentage of time spent sending snaps vs opening snaps out of total send+open time. Round to 2 decimal places.
question.ta: Prathi age group-ku, total send+open time-la send-ku evlo percentage, open-ku evlo percentage nu calculate pannu. 2 decimal places-ku round pannu.
question.hi: Har age group ke liye, total send+open time mein se snaps bhejne aur kholne ka percentage nikalo. 2 decimal places mein round karo.
question.te: Prathi age group ki, total send+open time lo snap pamputaniki evvari percentage, telupataniki evvari percentage calculate cheyyali. 2 decimal places ki round cheyyali.

title.ta: Tables join panni 'chat'-a filter out pannu
title.hi: Tables join karo aur 'chat' ko filter karo
title.te: Tables join chesi 'chat' ni filter out cheyyali

steps.sql:
SELECT a.user_id,
       ab.age_bucket,
       a.activity_type,
       a.time_spent
FROM activities a
JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open');

en: Two separate tables hold the data we need: activities has every user action (send, open, chat) with time spent, while age_breakdown maps each user to their age group. Neither table alone can answer the question.
JOIN activities a JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id — this links every activity row to the age bucket of the user who performed it. Alias a = activities, ab = age_breakdown.
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open') — this removes all 'chat' rows entirely. The question only asks about sending vs opening, so chat time must not enter any calculation.
Why filter this early? If chat rows survive into the aggregation step, SUM(time_spent) will include chat time in the denominator — and the percentages will be completely wrong.
Result of this step: a clean joined dataset with only send and open rows, each tagged with the user's age bucket — ready for grouping.
ta: Rendu separate tables-la data irukku: activities-la prathi user action (send, open, chat) time-oda irukku. age_breakdown-la user-ku age group mapping irukku. Rendu tables-um venum.
JOIN activities a JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id — prathi activity row-ku antha user-oda age bucket link aagum. a = activities alias, ab = age_breakdown alias.
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open') — 'chat' rows-a completely remove panrom. Question-la send vs open mattum venum, so chat time calculation-la varakoodathu.
Yen early filter? Chat rows survive aagittna aggregation-la SUM(time_spent) denominator-la chat time kooduthum — percentage completely wrong aagum.
Indha step result: only send, open rows — prathi row-oda age bucket theriyum. Next step-ku ready.
hi: Do alag tables mein data hai: activities mein har user ki action (send, open, chat) aur time_spent hai. age_breakdown mein user ka age group mapping hai. Dono tables chahiye.
JOIN activities a JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id — har activity row ke saath us user ka age bucket jud jaata hai. a = activities alias, ab = age_breakdown alias.
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open') — 'chat' rows ko poori tarah hata dete hain. Question sirf send vs open ke baare mein hai, chat time kisi bhi calculation mein nahi aana chahiye.
Pehle filter kyun? Agar chat rows aggregation tak pahunch gayi toh SUM(time_spent) mein chat time aa jaayega — percentages bilkul galat ho jaayenge.
Is step ka result: sirf send aur open rows ka joined dataset — har row ke saath age bucket bhi hai. Agla step ke liye taiyaar.
te: Rendu separate tables lo data undi: activities lo prathi user action (send, open, chat) time_spent tho undi. age_breakdown lo user ki age group mapping undi. Rendu tables kavali.
JOIN activities a JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id — prathi activity row ki antha user age bucket link avutundi. a = activities alias, ab = age_breakdown alias.
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open') — 'chat' rows ni completely teyyali. Question lo send vs open matrame kavali, chat time ee calculation lo ravakoodadu.
Mundu filter endhuku? Chat rows aggregation varaku vasthe SUM(time_spent) denominator lo chat time vasthundi — percentages poortiga tappu avutaayi.
Ee step result: only send, open rows — prathi row tho age bucket kuda undi. Next step ki ready.

title.en: Group by age and split send vs open time using CASE WHEN
title.ta: Age-wise group panni CASE WHEN use panni send vs open time split pannu
title.hi: Age ke hisaab se group karo aur CASE WHEN se send vs open time alag karo
title.te: Age wise group chesi CASE WHEN use chesi send vs open time split cheyyali

steps.sql:
SELECT ab.age_bucket,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'send'
               THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END) AS send_time,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'open'
               THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END) AS open_time
FROM activities a
JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open')
GROUP BY ab.age_bucket
ORDER BY ab.age_bucket;

en: GROUP BY ab.age_bucket collapses all rows of the same age group into a single row. All three 21-25 users become one row, all 26-30 become one row, and so on.

CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'send' THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END — for each row, if it is a send activity, use its time_spent value; otherwise contribute 0. SUM() then adds all these values together per group.
This technique is called conditional aggregation — splitting a single column's values into multiple output columns based on a condition, all within one GROUP BY query. No subquery or JOIN needed.
The same logic applies for open: SUM(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'open' THEN time_spent ELSE 0 END) gives total open time per age group.
Run this step to verify: for 21-25 you should see send_time = 16.50, open_time = 15.10. For 26-30: send = 20.50, open = 7.80. For 31-35: send = 11.00, open = 20.30.
These are raw totals, not percentages yet. The next step converts them into rounded percentages.
ta: GROUP BY ab.age_bucket — same age group-oda ella rows-a oru single row-a collapse pannum. 21-25 users ellam oru row, 26-30 ellam oru row, ippadi.
CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'send' THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END — prathi row-ku: activity 'send'-a? time_spent use pannu. Illana 0 kudukku. SUM() prathi group-la indha values-a ellam add pannum.
Ithu conditional aggregation technique — oru column-oda values-a condition based-a multiple output columns-a split panra method. Oru GROUP BY query-la pannalam, subquery veiyaadhu.
Same logic open-ku: SUM(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'open' THEN time_spent ELSE 0 END) — age group-wise total open time kitechu.
Indha step run panni verify pannu: 21-25-ku send_time = 16.50, open_time = 15.10. 26-30: send = 20.50, open = 7.80. 31-35: send = 11.00, open = 20.30.
Ivi raw totals — percentage illai. Next step-la convert pannuvom.
hi: GROUP BY ab.age_bucket — same age group ki saari rows ek single row mein collapse ho jaati hain. 21-25 ke teeno users ek row, 26-30 ke ek row, aur aage aise.
CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'send' THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END — har row ke liye: agar 'send' hai toh time_spent lo, warna 0 do. SUM() har group ke andar ye saari values jod deta hai.
Yeh technique conditional aggregation kehlati hai — ek column ki values ko condition ke basis pe alag-alag output columns mein split karna, sirf ek GROUP BY query mein. Koi subquery nahi chahiye.
Yahi logic 'open' pe bhi: SUM(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'open' THEN time_spent ELSE 0 END) — har age group ka total open time mil jaata hai.
Is step ko run karo aur verify karo: 21-25 ke liye send_time = 16.50, open_time = 15.10. 26-30: send = 20.50, open = 7.80. 31-35: send = 11.00, open = 20.30.
Ye sirf raw totals hain, percentage nahi. Agla step inhe rounded percentages mein convert karega.

Ivi raw totals — percentages kaadu. Next step lo convert chestaam.

title.en: Calculate percentages and round to 2 decimal places
title.ta: Percentage calculate panni 2 decimal places-ku round pannu
title.hi: Percentages calculate karo aur 2 decimal places mein round karo
title.te: Percentages calculate chesi 2 decimal places ki round cheyyali

steps.sql:
SELECT ab.age_bucket,
       ROUND(
         SUM(CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'send'
                 THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END) * 100.0
         / SUM(a.time_spent), 2
       ) AS send_perc,
       ROUND(
         SUM(CASE WHEN a.activity_type = 'open'
                 THEN a.time_spent ELSE 0 END) * 100.0
         / SUM(a.time_spent), 2
       ) AS open_perc
FROM activities a
JOIN age_breakdown ab ON a.user_id = ab.user_id
WHERE a.activity_type IN ('send', 'open')
GROUP BY ab.age_bucket
ORDER BY ab.age_bucket;

en: Percentage formula: send_perc = send_time / (send_time + open_time) × 100. Since we already filtered out chat with WHERE IN ('send','open'), SUM(a.time_spent) is automatically equal to send_time + open_time. No need to write them separately in the denominator.

Why multiply by 100.0 and NOT 100? SQL integer division truncates: 11 / 31 = 0, not 0.35. Writing 100.0 forces the division result to be a decimal (float). Without this, every percentage would come out as 0.
ROUND(expression, 2) wraps the entire percentage formula and trims the result to exactly 2 decimal places. The second argument is the precision — how many digits after the decimal point you want.
The same formula works for open_perc: SUM(CASE WHEN 'open') * 100.0 / SUM(time_spent). For every age group, send_perc + open_perc will always add up to exactly 100.00.
ORDER BY ab.age_bucket sorts the output alphabetically by age group — 21-25 first, then 26-30, then 31-35.
Expected result: 21-25 → send 52.22%, open 47.78% | 26-30 → send 72.44%, open 27.56% | 31-35 → send 35.14%, open 64.86%. Older users open more, younger users send more.

Yen 100.0, 100 illai? SQL integer division truncate pannum: 11 / 31 = 0, 0.35 illai. 100.0 eludhina result decimal (float) aagum. Illana every percentage 0-a varum.
ROUND(expression, 2) — percentage formula-a fully wrap panni, result-a exactly 2 decimal places-ku round pannum. 2nd argument precision — decimal-ku appuram evlo digits nu solluchu.
Same formula open_perc-ku: SUM(CASE WHEN 'open') * 100.0 / SUM(time_spent). Prathi age group-ku send_perc + open_perc = exactly 100.00 varum.
